title: Duha, the forenoon prayer
hookLine: a voluntary prayer when the sun is up
carry: two units of duha thank every joint

lines: NOBODY IS REQUIRED TO PRAY IT.
cards: "By the morning hours." That's how Pickthall opens surah ninety-three, and the Arabic word behind those morning hours is today's word. Duha is not dawn.
Dawn has its prayer, fajr, prayed in the gray before sunrise. Duha comes later: the sun fully up, the commute done, the first coffee gone, the inbox filling.
The middle of the morning, the stretch easiest to stop noticing. Islam puts a prayer there too, and nobody is required to pray it.

teach.b: Duha is a voluntary prayer, prayed after the sun has risen well into the sky and before the heat of noon. Its smallest form is two units. First, the hour has a surah.
Surah ninety-three swears by the morning hours and the stillness of the night, then tells the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that his Lord has not left him.

A report in Sahih al-Bukhari ties it to a time when he had fallen ill and missed his night prayers, and someone taunted him that he'd been abandoned. So the forenoon, in that surah, is a sign of being remembered.
Second, a hadith in Sahih Muslim gives the prayer a surprising job. Every morning, it says, a charity is owed for each joint of your body.
Every glorifying of God is a charity, every word of praise, every good deed urged and every wrong discouraged. And two units prayed in the forenoon are enough for all of it.
Your knuckles, your knees, your jaw: two units cover the thanks. Third, a witness.
Umm Hani reported that on the day Mecca was opened, he bathed in her house and prayed eight units in the forenoon, lighter than any prayer she'd seen from him, yet with full bowing and prostration.
Fourth, the timing has a picture.

teach.h: WHEN YOUNG CAMELS FEEL THE HEAT.
teach.b: Another report in Sahih Muslim calls it the prayer of those who often turn back to God, and says its time is when the young camels feel the heat of the sand.
Scholars give the window in hours and minutes now; the hadith gives it in hot sand.

how: Muslims who keep the duha prayer pray at least two voluntary units after the sun has risen well and before the time of the noon prayer, often at work, at home, or in the mosque after a morning class.

o: the noon prayer, prayed when the sun is at its height
the mid-morning hours, and the voluntary prayer prayed in them
the dawn prayer, prayed in the gray light before sunrise

games.q: the forenoon prayer — tap the pairs.
p: eight units, the day Mecca was opened
feel the heat of the sand

s: duha is another name for the dawn prayer
dawn has fajr. duha comes later, when the sun is well up.
a hadith says two units of duha cover the charity owed for every joint
Sahih Muslim: every joint owes a charity each morning, and two units in the forenoon suffice.
duha is one of the five required prayers
it's voluntary, and its smallest form is two units.

games.q: every morning, the hadith says, you owe a charity for each joint in your body. what does it say covers all of it?
o: one large gift to the poor, once a year.
two units prayed in the forenoon.
games.why: Sahih Muslim 720: glorifying, praise and good deeds are each charities, and two units prayed in the forenoon suffice for it all.

practice: Slowly open and close your hands, roll your shoulders, flex your feet: each joint is one of the charities the hadith counts. If you pray, you can plan two units of duha for later this morning, or pray them now if the sun is up.
If you don't, let each joint you move be one thank-you, said without words.

wordCard.voice: Duha. The forenoon, when the sun is well up, and the voluntary prayer prayed in it. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the forenoon, when the sun is well up. surah 93, ad-Duha, takes its name from it.

carryVoice: Your line: two units of duha thank every joint. The morning is remembered, and so are you. That's today, done.
